terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the shelf after each task.

tasks.title: Read the end of the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/arrays.js`, make `lastOnShelf(shelf)` return the last scent of `shelf`, however many scents it holds, and leave `shelf` as it was. An empty shelf gives `'Empty shelf'`.

Check calls `lastOnShelf` with shelves of its own, of different lengths, one scent and none included, then makes sure the shelf it handed in still has all its scents.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on positions and length.
Handle the empty shelf first, by asking about its length.
Work out the last position from the length, so it fits a shelf of any size.
Run the file: the first line should name the last scent of today's shelf.
hints: A shelf of four scents and a shelf of nine have their last scent at different positions. The one thing that tells you where is the length.
Positions count from 0, so the last position is one less than the length. Reading a position the list does not have gives undefined, which is what an empty shelf would give.
The function has the shape `if (shelf.length === 0) { return 'Empty shelf' }`, then `return shelf[...]` with the last position worked out from `shelf.length`.

tasks.title: Restock a scent
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make `restock(shelf, scent)` put `scent` at the end of `shelf`, unless the shelf has it already: a scent is never on the shelf twice. Either way it returns how many scents are on the shelf now.

Check calls `restock` with shelves of its own and looks at the number that comes back and at the shelf afterwards, with a scent that is new and one that is there already.
nextSteps: Ask whether the shelf already has the scent.
When it does not, add the scent at the end of the shelf.
After that, give back how many scents the shelf holds.
Run the file and look at the line for Task 2.
hints: Two list tools from the lesson do this job: one answers whether a list holds a value, the other adds at the end.
`includes` gives back true or false, which an `if` can ask. The `!` in front of a question turns true into false. The count comes from the shelf's length after adding.
The function has the shape `if (!shelf.includes(scent)) { shelf.push(scent) }`, then `return shelf.length`.

tasks.title: Sell from the end
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `sellLast(shelf)` take the last scent off `shelf` and return `'Sold '` followed by its name, like `'Sold Amber'`. An empty shelf gives `'Nothing to sell'`.

Check calls `sellLast` with shelves of its own, an empty one included, and looks at the text that comes back and at the shelf afterwards: it must have lost its last scent and nothing else.
nextSteps: Handle the empty shelf first.
Take the last scent off the shelf, and keep what comes off.
Give back the text with that scent's name in it.
Run the file: the line for Task 3 should name the scent Task 2 added.
hints: Reading the last position only looks at a scent. The task takes it off the shelf too, and one list tool does both at once.
`pop()` takes the last item off a list and gives it back. Each call takes one more, so call it once and keep its answer in a `const`.
After the empty check, `const scent = shelf.pop()`, then return `'Sold '` joined to `scent`.

tasks.title: Find a scent's spot
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make `shelfSpot(shelf, scent)` return `'Sage is in spot 2'` for a scent on the shelf, with the spot counted from 1 the way the shop counts, and `'No Pine on the shelf'` for one that is not there. When a scent is there twice, the spot of the first one counts.

Check calls `shelfSpot` with shelves of its own: a scent in the first spot, in the last, twice, and not there at all.
nextSteps: Find the position of the scent with the list tool from the lesson.
Ask whether it was found, using the answer that means not found.
Turn the position into the shop's spot number, which starts at 1.
Run the file and try a scent that is not on today's shelf.
hints: One list tool gives back where a value is, counting from 0, and a special number when it is not there at all.
`indexOf` gives -1 when the value is missing. Ask about -1 exactly: a scent in the first spot has position 0, and 0 counts as false in an `if`.
Keep `shelf.indexOf(scent)` in a `const`, return the not-there text when it is `-1`, and otherwise build the text with the position plus 1.

tasks.title: Add up the day
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 5`, first write a function of your own, `isRefund(cents)`: it returns `true` when `cents` is below 0, and `false` otherwise. It only helps `takings`, so it stays off the export line.

Then make `takings(amounts)` return the sum of the sales in `amounts`, leaving the refunds out. Go through `amounts` with `for...of` and ask `isRefund` about each one. An empty day takes 0.

Check calls `isRefund` with amounts of its own, 0 included, then `takings` with days of its own, an empty day and a day of only refunds included. It also makes sure `takings` uses `isRefund` and `for...of`.
nextSteps: Write `isRefund` from the word `function` to its closing brace, under the comment for Task 5.
In `takings`, start a sum at 0 before the loop.
Go through the amounts with `for...of` and add each one that is not a refund.
Give the sum back after the loop and run the file.
hints: This is the `for...of` loop from the issue on loops, going over a list instead of a text, with a sum that grows each round.
A sum needs a starting value, or the first addition gives NaN. The return goes after the loop: inside it, the function would end in the first round.
`isRefund` is one line: `return cents < 0`. In `takings`, inside `for (const cents of amounts)`, add `cents` to the sum when `!isRefund(cents)`.
